T062.statement: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a root in $\mathbb C$.

T102.statement: For a real symmetric matrix $A$ and any invertible real matrix $P$, the matrices $A$ and $P^TAP$ have the same numbers of positive, negative and zero eigenvalues.
T102.reason: Inertia is invariant under congruence of quadratic forms, not a vague change of matrix basis.

T149.statement: If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]\times[c,d]$, then $\displaystyle\int_a^b\!\int_c^d f(x,y)\,dy\,dx=\int_c^d\!\int_a^b f(x,y)\,dx\,dy=\iint_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}f$.
T149.note: This card gives the continuous Riemann-integral case taught in Calc 3. The date 1907 refers to Fubini’s more general integration theorem.
T149.reason: State a precise course-appropriate case with all hypotheses, and distinguish its formulation from the dated general theorem.
